nodes.procedure: Firstly, 1 g TiO2 and 40 mg carbon black were ball-milled for 10 h to form a uniform mixture. Subsequently, the mixture was annealed at 1150°C for 3.5 h to obtain Ti4O7 powder.

nodes.name: Wet chemical reduction
nodes.procedure: Ru-loaded Ti₄O₇ was prepared by simple wet reduction. First, 60 mg Ti₄O₇ and RuCl₃ were evenly dispersed in 50 ml of deionized water. Subsequently, 7 mL of 1 M NaBH₄ solution was slowly added dropwise into the mixture with vigorous stirring. After stirring for 4 h, the product was collected by centrifugation and dried under vacuum at 60°C for 12 h. The obtained powder was further annealed at 300°C, 400°C, and 500°C for 1 h in the Ar atmosphere. The mass of Ti₄O₇ was maintained at 60 mg, and the dosage of RuCl₃ was changed to 20 mg, 40 mg, and 60 mg to achieve different Ru loading.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images of Ru/Ti4O7 show uniform coating by Ru NPs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) ... images display the uniform coating of the titanium oxide supports by Ru NPs with a size of ~10 nm (Figs. 2b and 1c).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images show Ru NPs (~10 nm) uniformly coated on titanium oxide supports including Ru/Ti4O7.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images display the uniform coating of the titanium oxide supports by Ru NPs with a size of ~10 nm (Figs. 2b and 1c).

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-HRTEM of Ru/Ti4O7 shows tight nanoscale binding and smooth interface transition between phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In aberration-corrected high-resolution (AC-HRTEM) of Ru / Ti_4 O_7, tight binding and appropriate matching at the nanoscale between the different phases can be observed, accompanied by a smooth transition at the interface (Fig. 2d).

nodes.characterization_summary: Simulated HAADF-STEM images match experimental results for Ti4O7 and Ru crystal structures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The simulated High Angle toroidal dark field image-scanning transmission electron microscope (HAADF-STEM) images obtained through the crystal structure of Ti_4 O_7 and Ru show remarkable agreement with the experimental results (Figs. 2e and 1f).

nodes.characterization_summary: Lattice spacing of 0.377 nm attributed to (102) plane of Ti4O7 and 0.234 nm to (100) plane of Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Based on these atomic images, the lattice spacing of 0.377 nm can be attributed to the (102) plane of Ti_4 O_7 (JCPDS 50-0787), while the lattice spacing of 0.234 nm corresponds to the (100) plane of Ru (JCPDS 89-4903, Figs. 2g, 1h, and Supplementary Fig. 7).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS-mapping shows uniform distribution of Ru, Ti, and O elements in Ru/Ti4O7.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ru, Ti, and O elements are uniformly distributed in the energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS)-mapping of Ru/Ti_4 O_7 (Fig. 2i).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern shows characteristic diffraction peaks of both Ru and Ti4O7.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the characteristic diffraction peaks assigned to Ru and Ti_4 O_7 coexist in the X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern (Fig. 2j).

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR spectra show increasing oxygen vacancy concentration trend from Ru/TiO2 to Ru/Ti4O7 to Ru/TiO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The oxygen vacancy concentration in Ru / TiO_2, Ru / Ti_4 O_7, and Ru/TiO shows an increasing trend due to the different stoichiometric ratios of Ti and O (Fig. 3a).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ti 2p/Ru 3p overlap and Ti 2p shift to higher binding energy in Ru-loaded titanium oxides indicate electron donation to Ru; Ru 3d in Ru/Ti4O7 shows Ru-O and Ru-Ru signals for Ti-O-Ru units.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) fine spectra of Ru/TiO_2, Ru / Ti_4 O_7, and Ru / TiO, the Ti 2p and Ru 3p regions display close overlap (Fig. 3b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES shows different white line intensities; Ru/Ti4O7 closest to Ru foil. Ti pre-K-edge shifts to higher energy in Ru/Ti4O7.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES), the Ru K-edge also exhibits different white line peak intensity after contacting with various titanium oxide supports (Fig. 3d).

nodes.characterization_summary: k²-weighted EXAFS shows weak Ru-O signal at 1.92 Å for Ru/TiO2 and Ru/Ti4O7; wavelet transform confirms Ti-O-Ru interface units.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra of Ru corresponding k²-weighted EXAFS Fourier transform spectra display a weak Ru–O signal located at 1.92 Å after contacting with TiO_2 or Ti_4 O_7 (Fig. 3e).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/Ti4O7 exhibits highest double-layer capacitance Cdl of 68.95 mF cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ru / Ti_4 O_7 exhibits the highest double-layer capacitance (C_dl) value (68.95 mF cm⁻²) with the same Ru loading.
